title: Four-Class Alzheimer MRI Classification
summary: A four-class TensorFlow MRI study that raised classification accuracy from 78% to 85% through CNN ensemble comparison and error analysis.
landingDeck: A linked-notebook classification study covering 6,400 MRI files, 256×256 preprocessing, an 80/10/10 split, CNN training, error analysis, and ensemble gains from 78% to 85% accuracy.
landingHighlights: Loads four folder-defined classes: NonDemented, VeryMildDemented, MildDemented, and ModerateDemented.
Builds a TensorFlow/Keras image pipeline with resizing, rescaling, augmentation, and train/validation/test partitions.
Reports a seven-point accuracy gain, from a 78% single-model baseline to an 85% ensemble result, in the linked companion notebook.
problem: The experiment tests whether convolutional models can distinguish four dementia-stage folders from MRI images while keeping the image pipeline and model variants inspectable in one notebook.
approach: The Colab notebook loads 6,400 image files, resizes them to 256×256, creates an 80/10/10 split, applies augmentation, trains convolutional networks, and averages prediction probabilities across model variants.
output: A linked set of Colab experiments covering dataset loading, sample inspection, preprocessing, CNN training, error analysis, and two- and three-model ensemble comparison.

methodology.evaluation: The companion experiment record reports 78% baseline accuracy and 85% ensemble accuracy on the study's held-out split. The current public notebook retains the pipeline and ensemble code, while its saved model.evaluate outputs are incomplete.
methodology.boundary: The dataset is referenced through an external Google Drive path. Subject-level separation, class counts by partition, external validation, and clinical review are not established by the repository.

role: I built the data-loading, preprocessing, augmentation, CNN, and ensemble experiments recorded in the notebook.
